item: The shutdown writes the -wal back before it disposes the pool, and the previous-session text says when it was left
status: built (draft PR; the 17 Oct local bundle rebased onto main, folded with the independent read of 26 Oct)
refs: PR #1475; coordinator 17 Oct 11:21: diff list approved as a local bundle, re-gated on main after #1429 and #1435 merged, D1 no time cap, D2 a straggler inside a read leaves the log and records it, the text must say the log was left; coordinator 26 Oct 06:39: R201 (one report member with reason codes, measured, the pin does not move), R202 (the early dispose stays, a count after it says so), M1 default, L1-L8 all fold
summary: The 10-10 session ended clean and left a 1.41 GB -wal (90.8 s of the next unlock). Engine.dispose() closes only the pool's idle connections and SQLite writes the log back when the LAST connection closes, so one connection still checked out leaves 100 % of it (measured: 300 MiB, SQLite 3.45.1 plain and sqlcipher3 0.6.2 [SQLite 3.51.1, SQLCipher 4.12.0] encrypted, straggler idle or inside a read). The lifespan now stamps a writing-back phase and runs one no-wait PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE) from a connection of its own (busy_timeout 0 first), between the storage guard's stop and the disposal, with the library swap lock's shared level held across the open, the checkpoint and the close, so a restore or repair swap cannot land mid-step and have this connection's close remove the new file's -wal by name. With an idle straggler it empties the log (2.2 s for 300 MiB). With a straggler inside a read the answer is busy in one of two shapes (26 Oct, plain, 214 MB log): a reader snapshot OLDER than every frame returns (1, n, 3) at once with nothing copied; a snapshot NEWER than the frames (the common shape) has TRUNCATE copy every frame first (1.1 to 1.4 s) and only then find the reader, so the contents are written back, the answer is still busy and the file keeps its size until the reader's close removes it (107 MB: 0.07 s); busy is also a writer or another checkpoint. The record carries whether every frame was copied. dispose_engine() returns the pool's own checked-out count, and says an earlier disposal replaced the pool (never 0) after the in-app power button or the unlock path disposed first. The sentinel keeps ONE dispose record (wal bytes after the disposal, connections out, the step's outcome, each a number or a code of at most seven characters), the report carries it as one member with the teardown's seconds computed at read time, a death inside the step reads unclean-end-during-write-back, and the Previous session text says 'the -wal was LEFT by that session's end: N bytes' whatever the verdict (it no longer prints "'clean' above" under a verdict that is not clean, and the not-measured line still says what the write-back did). The step and the record read the one path the connection creator opens (session.DB_FILE) and a non-SQLite backend is a named skip. BYTES: the member's worst case is 75 B built by the real reader at every cut (a 12-digit log size, 7-character codes, a 4-digit duration), crashing_thread_kind is now built by the real constants (eleven places of 37 B = 407 B, where 440 B was typed), the whole room sums to 2,415 B with 0 B unspent, and the 1,500,000 B diagnostics floor does not move; the first version of the member measured 253 B against 42 B free. Deviation from the diff list: the unlock path's _close_after_checkpoint is untouched (a separate helper). Not changed: src/safety/shutdown.py's early dispose before SIGTERM (R202: it stays; dropping it is 0.5.1 open item 25). A kill in the middle of the step reads as an unclean end during the write-back, which is true. tests/test_shutdown_wal.py: 45 tests, plain and encrypted; red without each of: PASSIVE for TRUNCATE, no zero busy timeout, the swap lock around the step, the copied-all arithmetic (always false; without its n>0 guard), the earlier-disposal memory, the copied code, the writing-back stamp, its verdict and its session-history state (10 scratch mutations, each killed by a test). NOT measured: that a next open's recovery copies a log the step left a second time.
